ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $4.19 Ryde voucher to the rider for the unexempted off-route extra distance (RD-2); leave the $1.15 metered waiting time and the rest of the metered fare unchanged; no account action against the driver.
ruling.reasoning:
Segment F4 (12:25–12:36, 4.57 km driven vs 1.60 km optimal, extra 2.97 km, straying up to 729 m off the corridor) is the sole off-route segment, so it is reviewed segment-by-segment under RD-1 [F4]. The code trace settles RD-4 as failing: no incident on the replaced optimal stretch, only PAN ISLAND EXPRESSWAY band 5 and CENTRAL EXPRESSWAY band 4 during the window and fair weather, and a band record alone cannot exempt (RD-4(b)) [F13][F14][F15][F16][RD-4].

RD-3(a) turns on the rider's own pre-segment message: at 12:21 she named a specific place — "Can you stop at Paya Lebar Square?" — the driver accepted ("Ok can"), and the car stopped there (F2, stationary 4 min 0 s at 12:28–12:32) [F9][F10][F2][RD-3]. Because the rider named the place and the car stopped there, the driving to reach that stop is not a detour and its extra km are exempt in full; the segment is not split into the stop and the way there [F4][F9][RD-3]. RD-3(b) applies only where the rider did not name a place and the driver chose the location, which is not this case, so on RD-3 the single segment F4 is exempt.

RD-5 is the harder branch and I read the words: the rider's 12:21 message asked for a 3–4 minute stop, not a route or a routing change [F9][F10]. For the half of the segment that is the way to her named stop, RD-3(a) exempts the whole way there; for the routing itself there is no rider message before 12:25:20 agreeing to any route, and the driver's post-trip statement that he "drove there and waited" is a driver-side claim about a verbal arrangement, not consent (G11) [F12][RD-5]. The chat is complete and timestamped (F11), so the record settles that the rider gave no route agreement; what remains is the measured surplus the trace computes, 2.97 km of extra distance within F4 [F4][F11][RD-5].

The consequence is refund_partial under RD-2 for this metered RydeTAXI trip: refund = extra_km of the non-exempt segment × this trip's per-km rate = distance fare ÷ distance km = $26.72 ÷ 18.95 km = $1.4100/km, so 2.97 km × $1.4100/km = $4.1877, rounded to $4.19 [F4][F8][RD-2]. The billed excess-distance line is $4.91 (3.48 km × $1.4100/km); RD-2 refunds only the unexempted segment's extra_km and expressly does not refund the remaining corridor-return and map-matching mileage, so the refundable amount is $4.19 [F5][F8][F4][RD-2]. The $1.15 metered waiting time (4.4 min × $0.26/min) is chargeable on RydeTAXI and is not refunded [F6][F2][RD-3]. No account action attaches: the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days and profile facts cannot decide the case alone, so there is no repeated-breach predicate [F18][F17][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages (F9, F10) and the driver's statement (F12) in context — a parcel-stop arrangement and an ordinary fare complaint, with no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F9][F10][F12][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

Evidence: the record settles every element the ruling needs — one measured off-route segment with kilometre figures, the complete timestamped chat (F11), the fare breakdown with the per-km rate, and the driver statement; no record is missing or untimed, so no evidence gap arises [F4][F8][F11][F12].

Accepted: the stationary period is the rider's named parcel stop and the $1.15 metered waiting time is chargeable, not refundable [F2][F6][F9][RD-3].
